author_route: OpenCodex, as stated by the parent dispatch; the route was not checked separately in this session
purpose: Comparator condition 'STE applied Korean' in a 1:1:1 comparison (untreated Korean / Korean Protocol Korean / STE applied Korean) on the same inputs.
condition_definition: This condition applies English ASD-STE100 writing principles to Korean. It does not claim conformance to the official English STE dictionary.

independence.not_read: Korean Protocol rules, profiles, evaluation cases, gold data, condition keys, and model outputs in this directory were not opened.
independence.excluded_from_profile: The user example '표기된 담당자 없음' and any Korean Protocol special guards were left out on purpose.

sources.access: Paraphrase and locators from the earlier verified extract in sourceevidence.json; not downloaded again

rules_used.4.2: Do not omit words to make sentences shorter.
rules_used.4.5: Keep necessary articles/demonstratives; repeated articles mark modifier scope. Mapped to Korean only as 'keep words needed for scope and reference', not as adding 이/그.
rules_used.5.2: One instruction per sentence unless actions are simultaneous.
rules_used.5.4: Put a condition the reader must know first before the instruction.

principles_used: Each approved word has one meaning; one synonym is selected (basis for consistent terms, no synonyms).
Technical nouns and technical verbs come from official documentation, drawings, glossaries; do not invent them.
Short sentences, one topic per sentence, active voice.
Procedures use direct imperative language, are not narrative, and do not use the passive; descriptive text uses active voice; passive is allowed only when the agent is unknown.
A condition the reader must know before a step goes at the start of the sentence.
STE covers procedural and descriptive texts and safety instructions (warnings, cautions).

sources.used_for: Profile rule 20: case particles may be omitted when recoverable and meaning is unchanged; auxiliary particles carry meaning.
Profile rule 20: a subject recoverable from context may be omitted.

1-4: STE-FAQ (no invented content is a preservation constraint of this comparison)

adaptation_choices.choice: Neutral plain style (-다) without honorifics; the requested genre and quotations keep their original style.
adaptation_choices.basis: Experiment design choice to match the Korean Protocol condition style for a fair comparison. This is not an STE rule.

adaptation_choices.choice: Instructions use the plain -ㄴ다/-는다 ending as the Korean rendering of the STE imperative.
adaptation_choices.basis: Language adaptation. STE 5.3 defines the English imperative only.

adaptation_choices.choice: Recoverable Korean subject and case-particle omission is allowed only when who, what, condition, and modality stay clear.
adaptation_choices.basis: Korean language adaptation supported by NIKL answers. STE 4.2 forbids English word omission and does not license Korean omission.

adaptation_choices.choice: English STE sentence word limits are not applied to Korean eojeol counts.
adaptation_choices.basis: Word and eojeol counts are not comparable units; length is controlled through one topic and one instruction per sentence.

adaptation_choices.choice: No Korean mapping of STE approved words is claimed.
adaptation_choices.basis: The STE dictionary is English. Profile rules 5-7 keep only the one-name-one-meaning principle.

limitations: This profile is a Korean comparator built on STE principles. It cannot serve as evidence of formal STE equivalence or conformance.

Rule locators come from the earlier extract in sourceevidence.json and the public FAQ. The full 434-page standard was not re-read in this session, so other STE rules (noun clusters, verb forms, punctuation, safety-instruction format details) are summarized only at the FAQ level.
The profile was written by one author model without a separate review or pilot run.
NIKL online Q&A answers are case explanations and are published only for about two years.

changes: Aligned task framing with generation requests rather than forcing editing.
Clarified selecting an existing name when multiple aliases refer to one item; identifiers remain unchanged.
